blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment)
s: A detached retina is when the thin layer at the back of your eye (retina) becomes loose.
It needs to be treated quickly to stop it permanently affecting your sight.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Symptoms of a detached retina
s: Symptoms of a detached retina include:

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Symptoms of a detached retina
s: floaters (dots and lines) or flashes of light in your eye

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Symptoms of a detached retina
s: a dark "curtain" or shadow in your vision

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Symptoms of a detached retina
s: changes to your eyesight, such as blurred vision

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Urgent advice: Get help from NHS 111 if:
s: floaters (dots and lines) suddenly appear in your vision or suddenly increase in number

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Urgent advice: Get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you get flashes of light in your vision

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Urgent advice: Get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have a dark "curtain" or shadow moving across your vision

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Urgent advice: Get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your vision gets suddenly blurred

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Urgent advice: Get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: You'll be referred to hospital for surgery if tests show your retina may be detached or has started to come away (retinal tear).

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: Surgery will usually stop your vision getting worse.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: What happens during surgery for a detached retina or tear

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: Surgery to re-attach the retina or fix a retinal tear may involve:

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: removing and replacing the jelly inside your eye (vitrectomy)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: attaching a small band around your eye to push the wall of your eye and retina closer together (scleral buckling)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: injecting a bubble of gas into your eye to push the retina against the back of your eye (pneumatic retinopexy)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: sealing the tear in your retina with laser or freezing treatment (cryotherapy)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: It's usually done with local anaesthetic, so you're awake but your eye is numbed.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: You do not normally need to stay in hospital overnight.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Treatment for a detached retina
s: You may be asked to lie or sit in a particular position for up to 7 days after the surgery.
This is so that your retina is in the correct position to help it heal.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: Recovery time after surgery for a detached retina varies.
But as a general guide, for 2 to 6 weeks after surgery:

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: your vision may be blurry

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: your eye may be sore and red – take paracetamol if you need to

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: you may need to take time off work

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: you may not be able to drive

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: you may need to avoid flying (if you've had a bubble of gas put into your eye)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina
s: Most people are eventually able to return to all their normal activities.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Recovering from a detached retina > Important
s: Call the hospital or go to A&E if the pain, redness or blurriness gets worse after surgery.
You may need further treatment.

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: A detached retina is usually caused by changes to the jelly inside your eye, which can happen as you get older.
This is called posterior vitreous detachment (PVD).

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: It's not clear exactly why PVD can lead to retinal detachment in some people and there's nothing you can do to prevent it.
But it's more likely to happen if you:

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: are short-sighted

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: have had an eye operation (such as cataract surgery)

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: have had an eye injury

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: have a family history of retinal detachment

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Causes of a detached retina
s: Find out more about posterior vitreous detachment from RNIB

blocks.path: Detached retina (retinal detachment) > Important: If your symptoms come back
s: You can get a detached retina more than once.
Get medical help as soon as possible if the symptoms come back.
